title: The Reinebold Report
subtitle: "Ninety-nine percent of this game is showing up. The other one percent is starting the right running back."
tagline: Week 11 — Seven Tenths Of A Point And A Tight End On A Beach Somewhere
author: Jeff Reinebold
lede: Gather round, gang, and bring a magnifying glass, because the Lambs beat the Done Dingos by 0.7. Seven tenths of a point. And the Dingos had Jordan Mason sitting on the bench with 4.7 while Emeka Egbuka gave 3.8 at FLEX. Do that one swap and the Dingos win by 0.2. Meanwhile Major Tuddy hung 171.16 on Cracked Out Uncle, the high of the week, and won by 68.7. Dak Prescott scored 35.9, the top starter in the league, and AllIGoneToPot made it three straight wins. Last week's 190-point juggernaut, False Hope, started Tucker Kraft on a bye week, got 0.0 from the Vikings D/ST a week after they scored 21.0, and left Ladd McConkey's 20.7 on the bench. Bang average remembered there are ten lineup spots and won by 37.32. And 1 season wonder put up 90.96, the low of the week, for a sixth straight loss. The Lambs are alone in first at 8-3. Film's loaded. Let's roll.

matchups.recap: The closest game since Week 7, decided by 0.7. The Lambs won it with their receivers on a milk carton. Ja'Marr Chase scored 8.1 on a 25.37 projection, Luther Burden III 3.3 and Ryan Flournoy 2.1 at FLEX. That's 13.5 points from three guys projected for 50.09, all of them healthy and just quiet. Emmett Johnson saved the day with 24.3, Jared Goff added 20.36, Derrick Henry 19.1 and Trey McBride 14.8. Perfect lineup, nothing on the bench worth a look, and a third straight win. Alone in first. The Dingos got 24.96 from Patrick Mahomes and 24.1 from Javonte Williams, and the Broncos D/ST scored 12.0 on a 6.46 projection. But Chase Brown gave 8.6, Bhayshul Tuten 8.3 and Egbuka 3.8 at FLEX, while Jordan Mason scored 4.7 on the bench. Mason for Egbuka is +0.9. They lost by 0.7. That lineup scores 116.26 and wins by 0.2. Gang, I've seen games lost on fumbles, on penalties, on fourth-and-inches. I've never seen one lost on nine tenths of a running back.
matchups.trashTalk: Done Dingos, last week you set a perfect lineup and won by 45. This week you missed it by one swap and lost by seven tenths. The dingo ate your baby, and then it ate your FLEX. Silence of the CeeDee Lambs, your receivers combined for 13.5 and you're in first place by yourself. The lambs were silent. They still won.

matchups.recap: The biggest margin of the week, 68.7, and the high score of the week, 171.16. CeeDee Lamb scored 30.2, Breece Hall 19.0, Tetairoa McMillan 19.1, Parker Washington 18.3, James Cook III 17.2, David Montgomery 15.4 and C.J. Stroud 20.46. Cam Little kicked 13.0. And the Steelers D/ST, which scored MINUS 7.0 last week, came back with plus 7.0. Exactly a fourteen-point swing in attitude. Perfect lineup. Mike Evans scored 22.9 on IR, which doesn't count, and nobody's mad about it. Cracked Out Uncle got 26.0 from Chuba Hubbard and then not much else. Courtland Sutton caught 0 balls on 2 targets for 0.0 at FLEX, Jaylen Warren gave 4.9 on a 15.65 projection and Jonathan Taylor 6.7 on 16.62. That's 11.6 points from three guys projected for 42.6. Drake London, Jordan Love and Matthew Golden all scored 0.0 on the bench, so there was nobody to call. Two straight losses after a six-game streak.
matchups.trashTalk: Cracked Out Uncle, two weeks ago you were the hottest team in the league. Now you've given up 1,599.2 points this season, the most in the league, and your FLEX had zero catches. The cult has run out of Kool-Aid. Major Tuddy, last week your defense scored for the other team. This week your defense showed up and the whole roster followed it. That's a Tuddy.

matchups.recap: Last week AllIGoneToPot started Brock Purdy and left Dak Prescott's 34.42 on the bench. This week they flipped the coin the other way, and Dak scored 35.9, the top starter in the league, while Purdy's 22.2 sat. That's 13.7 points of getting it right. One-QB league, you pick one, and this time they picked the one. Then Travis Kelce scored 25.4 on an 11.34 projection, Jameson Williams 19.3, Zay Flowers 16.4, and Dominic Zvada, who kicked 2.0 last week, kicked 15.0. DK Metcalf gave 1.2 at RB/WR on one catch for 2 yards, and Keenan Allen scored 6.8 on the bench, a 5.6-point swing they didn't need. Questionable or Kicked got 27.9 from Ashton Jeanty on a 14.11 projection, 18.5 from Malik Nabers and 15.0 from the Bears D/ST. But Isaiah Likely went from 27.7 last week to 4.5, Rome Odunze and Stefon Diggs gave 8.5 each, and Joe Burrow managed 19.9. Perfect lineup, 18.7-point loss. Kelce alone made up the margin.
matchups.trashTalk: AllIGoneToPot, three straight wins. I don't know what's in that pot, but I want the recipe. Questionable or Kicked, your name finally asked the right question, and the answer was kicked. Still the most points in the league, still a nice house, but somebody left the back door open.

matchups.recap: Bang average started ten players this week. All ten. I checked twice. And it worked: 154.66, a perfect lineup and a 37.32-point win. George Pickens followed up last week's 43.5 with 23.8, Bucky Irving scored 19.0, George Kittle 18.4, Justice Hill 17.6 on an 8.35 projection, and Tyler Bass kicked 17.0. The 49ers D/ST added 14.0 on a 5.39 projection. False Hope came down off the 190 hard. Jonah Coleman scored 34.9 on a 19.39 projection and DJ Moore 23.1, but Tucker Kraft started at TE on a Green Bay bye and scored 0.0, the Vikings D/ST went from 21.0 to 0.0, Jordyn Tyson gave 2.0 on one catch and one carry, and Garrett Wilson 6.9. Meanwhile Ladd McConkey, who gave 0.0 as a starter in Week 9, scored 20.7 on the bench. McConkey for Tyson is +18.7. The perfect lineup scores 136.04, which still loses by 18.62, so it wasn't the difference. It was just a lot of points to leave in a folding chair.
matchups.trashTalk: False Hope, you started a tight end whose team didn't play. That's not false hope, that's no hope, and it's printed right there on the NFL schedule. Bang average, ten starters, 154 points and a perfect lineup. That's the most above-average thing you've done all year. Somebody's going to have to change the name.

matchups.recap: Kelce's Wildest Dream Team snapped a two-game skid by 27.44 with a perfect lineup. Jahmyr Gibbs scored 27.8, Chris Olave 19.2 on a 14.15 projection, the Texans D/ST 15.0 and Colston Loveland 11.9. Bo Nix gave 11.5 on a 20.78 projection, Cam Skattebo 5.8 and Spencer Shrader kicked 1.0, but it didn't matter. And here's a twist for you: Jalen Coker and Omarion Hampton switched sides since last week. Coker scored 8.7 for the Dream Team against his old team, Hampton 10.3 for 1 season wonder. 1 season wonder scored 90.96, the low of the week. Josh Allen gave 12.16 on a 23.38 projection, Justin Jefferson 13.7, Will Reichard kicked 3.0 and Tyler Warren 3.2 with Dallas Goedert's 4.8 on the bench, a 1.6-point swing in a 27.44-point loss. Six straight losses.
matchups.trashTalk: 1 season wonder, the name keeps getting more accurate. Six straight losses, the low score of the week, and your quarterback scored 12. The wonder now is how. Kelce's Wildest Dream Team, your kicker scored 1.0 and you still won by 27. Even your nightmares are winning now.

awards.label: Stud of the Week
awards.note: Projected for 21.89, beat it by 14.01. The top starter in the league, one week after scoring 34.42 on the bench. AllIGoneToPot finally put him on the field and he paid for the ticket. Three straight wins.

awards.label: Workhorse Award
awards.note: Projected for 14.11 and nearly doubled it. Did his part and then some for Questionable or Kicked. Lost by 18.7 anyway. Workhorses don't pick the result, they just pull the cart.

awards.label: Bust of the Week
awards.note: Projected for 25.37, delivered 8.1 on 5 catches for 31 yards. No injury, just a quiet day. A shortfall of 17.27, the worst in the league, in a game the Lambs won by 0.7. That's more than 24 times the margin. He got away with it. Honorable mentions: Luther Burden III (3.3 on 15.08), Josh Allen (12.16 on 23.38) and Jaylen Warren (4.9 on 15.65).

awards.label: Bench Blunder
awards.note: Jordan Mason scored 4.7 on the bench while Emeka Egbuka gave 3.8 at FLEX. A +0.9 swing. They lost by 0.7. That lineup scores 116.26 and beats the Lambs' 116.06 by 0.2. The smallest bench blunder you'll ever see, and the one that cost a whole game. Honorable mention: False Hope left Ladd McConkey's 20.7 on the bench behind Jordyn Tyson's 2.0 (+18.7) and started Tucker Kraft on a bye, but they lost by 37.32, so that one was just ugly, not fatal.

awards.label: Defensive Disaster
awards.note: Projected for 4.47, delivered 0.0, the only defense in the league that didn't score. Last week they put up 21.0 for False Hope in a 190-point game. This week they put up nothing. Two weeks ago it was 6.0. Gang, I've seen more consistency from a weather forecast.

awards.label: Surprise of the Week
awards.note: Projected for 19.39, beat it by 15.51, the biggest jump over projection in the league. The second-best starter of the week, in a loss. Honorable mention: Travis Kelce scored 25.4 on an 11.34 projection for AllIGoneToPot. Not for the team named after him. Never for the team named after him.

momentOfWeek.text: Picture it, gang. Done Dingos versus the Lambs, and it comes down to the last decimal. The Dingos are at 115.36. The Lambs are at 116.06. Seven tenths of a point. You go back to the lineup to see what happened, and there it is. Emeka Egbuka at FLEX, projected for 10.91, gives you 3.8. And sitting right there on the bench, eligible, healthy, ready to go: Jordan Mason, 4.7. Nine tenths of a point better. Not a blowout. Not a star. Just a guy who would have caught one more pass than the other guy. Swap them and the Dingos win by 0.2. Instead they're 4-7, ninth in the standings, and their points for and points against are separated by 0.8 for the whole season. These guys are the most perfectly average losing team I've ever seen. Coaches, the little decisions are the big decisions. You just don't find out until Monday.
momentOfWeek.attribution: — from the film room, Coach Reinebold

powerRankings.take: Three straight wins and alone in first. Won by 0.7 with Chase at 8.1 and the FLEX at 2.1. Lucky or good? At 8-3, who cares.
High score of the week, 68.7-point win, perfect lineup. The defense that scored minus seven came back plus seven. Rolling.
Still lead the league in points (1,647.76), 117.78 clear of Tuddy. Lost to a team that read the QB depth chart right for once.
Two straight losses, a FLEX with zero catches, and 1,599.2 points allowed, the most in the league. The streak is a memory.
Ten starters, perfect lineup, 37.32-point win. Third in points (1,505.96) with a 5-6 record. The name is lying.
Three straight wins, Dak on the field, Kelce at 25.4. The pot is simmering.
190.58 one week, a bye-week tight end and 20.7 on the bench the next. The name is back to telling the truth.
Gibbs 27.8, a perfect lineup and a 27.44-point win. Four teams at 5-6 and they're one of them.
Lost by 0.7 with Mason's 4.7 on the bench. Points for 1,386.24, points against 1,385.44. Average in every way except the record.
Low of the week, six straight losses, fewest points in the league (1,290.4). The wonder season is long gone.

lastWord: That's Week 11, gang. A game decided by seven tenths of a point, with nine tenths sitting on the bench. A tight end started on a bye. A defense that went from 21.0 to 0.0. A defense that went from minus seven to plus seven. Dak finally off the bench and the top starter in the league. Bang average with all ten chairs filled. The Lambs alone in first at 8-3, Tuddy and Questionable or Kicked at 7-4, the Uncle at 6-5, four teams at 5-6, the Dingos at 4-7, and 1 season wonder at 3-8 with six straight losses. Check the bye weeks. Check the bench. And check it twice, because sometimes the whole game is hiding in a decimal. Reinebold out.
footerTagline: "Games are won by inches. Fantasy games are won by tenths."
